paragraphs.text: Form No. HCJD/C-121 ORDER SHEET IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT MULTAN BENCH, MULTAN JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT Case No. Crl. Misc.No.6707-M of 2026 Muhammad Nawaz Vs The State, etc. Sr. No. Date of order Order with signature of Judge, and that of parties or counsel, where necessary. 02.11.2026 Makhdoom Mashooq Hussain Shah, Advocate for the petitioner. Ms. Naheed Kanwal, Deputy District Public Prosecutor for the State/respondent No.1 and Medical Superintendent/respondent No.2. Rana Muhammad Nadeem Kanjoo, Advocate for respondent No.3 alongwith Tanveer, S.I. and record of the case. . Through this petition, Muhammad Nawaz (petitioner) has made following prayer:- “Under the above submissions, it is therefore, most respectfully prayed that this petition may very kindly be accepted and the impugned order dated 15.06.2026 passed by the Learned Lower Court may very graciously be set aside by declaring illegal, unlawful, contrary to law, facts, therefore, the same may very graciously be set aside and the order dated 21.05.2026 passed by the Learned Trial Court may very graciously be upheld in the supreme interest of justice. It is further prayed that the operation of impugned order dated 15.06.2026 passed by the Learned Lower Court may kindly be suspended till the final decision of the instant petition. Any other relief, which this Hon'ble Court deems fit, just and proper may also be awarded to the petitioner.”

Brief however necessary facts for disposal of instant petition are that Muhammad Nawaz (present petitioner) got registered F.I.R. No.379/2026 dated: 09.05.2026 under Sections: 337-A(i)(ii), 337-F(i)(v), 148, 149 PPC at police Station: Siray Sidhu, District Khanewal (copy of FIR is available at page No.14 of this petition as annexure-B) against accused persons namely Allah Yar (now arrayed as respondent No.3 in this petition) and others; Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed application before learned Area Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala for constituting medical board regarding Medico-Legal Examination Certificates bearing Nos. 104/2026, 105/2026, 106/2026 and 107/2026 of Muhammad Waseem, Faisal Nadeem, Muhammad Amir and Muhammad Nawaz (present petitioner) respectively, copy of the application is available at page Nos.15-16 of this petition as annexure-C, which was dismissed vide order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala (copy whereof is available at page No.17 of this petition as annexure-C/1); Allah Yar (mentioned above) filed revision petition against aforesaid order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala before learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala, which was allowed vide order dated: 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala (copy whereof is available at page Nos.22-24) and same has been impugned through instant petition.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that since order dated 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala (mentioned above) was an executive order, therefore, same cannot be challenged through revision petition and hence impugned order dated: 15.06.2026 passed in revision petition by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala is against the law and thus not sustainable and finally prays for setting aside the same.
On the other hand, learned counsel for Allah Yar/respondent No.3 while supporting the impugned order has vehemently opposed instant petition.

Learned Deputy District Public Prosecutor also submits that since order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala was an executive order, therefore, same cannot be challenged through revision petition and hence impugned order dated: 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala is not sustainable.
Arguments heard. Available record has been perused.

It is well settled that Magistrate is entrusted with diverse duties and acts in dual capacity i.e. as persona designata and as a Court. Though primary responsibility for conducting investigation of criminal case rests with the police, yet a Magistrate exercises supervisory functions in relation to certain aspects of the investigation. Some powers exercised and functions performed by a Magistrate are executive and administrative in nature, and while discharging such functions, the Magistrate does not act as Court but as a persona designata. Needless to observe that while entertaining an application seeking medical re-examination of an injured person, the Magistrate acts in the capacity of a persona designata and not as a Court; consequently, any order passed thereon is administrative/executive in nature. In this regard, case of “AHMAD KHAN versus ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, TALAGANG and 4 others” (PLD 2020 Lahore 77) can be safely referred. It is equally well settled that under Section: 435 Cr.P.C., the record of any proceedings before any inferior Criminal Curt may be called for and examined by the High Court or any Sessions Judge to satisfy itself or himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such inferior Court. When such record has been called for, the High Court is competent to exercise its revisional jurisdiction under Section: 439 Cr.P.C. whereas the learned Sessions Judge may exercise revisional jurisdiction under Section 439-A Cr.P.C. and for ready reference, said provisions of law are reproduced hereunder- “435. Power to call for records of inferior Courts. (1) The High Court or any Sessions Judge may call for and examine the record of any proceeding before any inferior Criminal Court situate within the local limits of its or his jurisdiction for the purpose of satisfying itself or himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order recorded or passed, and as to the regularity of any proceedings of such inferior Court and may, when calling for such record, direct that the execution of any sentence be suspended and, if the accused is in confinement, that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending examination of the record. 24[Explanation. All Magistrates, shall be deemed to be inferior to the Session Judge for the purposes of this sub-section.]” “439. High Court's powers of revision. (1) In the case of any proceeding the record of which has been called for by itself, [...] or which otherwise comes to its knowledge, the High Court may, in its discretion, exercise any of the powers conferred on a Court of Appeal by sections 423, 426, 427 and 428 or on a Court by section 338, and may enhance the sentence; and, when the Judges composing the Court of Revision are equally divided in opinion, the case shall be disposed of in manner provided by section 429. (2) No order under this section shall be made to the prejudice of the accused unless he has had an opportunity of being heard either personally or by pleader in his own defence. (3) Where the sentence dealt with under this section has been passed by Magistrate 34[...], the Court shall not inflict a greater punishment for the offence which, in the opinion of such Court, the accused has committed, than might have been inflicted for such offence by Magistrate of the first class. 35(4) Nothing in this section shall be deemed to authorize a High Court: (a) to convert a finding of acquittal into one of conviction; or (b) to entertain any proceedings in revision with respect to an order made by the Sessions Judge under section 439-A.] (5) Where under this Code an appeal lies and no appeal is brought, no proceedings by way of revision shall be entertained at the instance of the party who could have appealed. (6) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, any convicted person to whom an opportunity has been given under sub- section (2) of showing cause why his sentence should not be enhanced, shall, in showing cause, be entitled also to show cause against his conviction.” “36[439-A. Sessions Judge's powers of revision. (1) In the case of any proceeding before a Magistrate the record of which has been called for by the Sessions Judge or which otherwise comes to his knowledge, the Sessions Judge may exercise any of the powers conferred on the High Court by section 439. (2) An Additional Sessions Judge shall have and may exercise all the powers of a Sessions Judge under this Chapter in respect of any case which may be transferred to him under any general or special order of the Session Judge].” Bare perusal of aforementioned Sections: 435, 439 and 439-A, Cr.P.C. reveals that record of any proceedings before any inferior Criminal Court may be called and examined by the High Court or Sessions Judge, as the case may be, for the purpose of satisfying itself or himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order recorded or passed, and as to regularity of any proceedings of such Court. And the revisional jurisdiction of High Court and any Sessions Judge, however, is confined to the proceedings of, and orders emanating from an inferior Criminal Court. Admittedly, while conducting proceedings on an application seeking medical re-examination of an injured, the Magistrate does not act as a Criminal Court but in the capacity of a persona designata. Consequently, the order dated: 21.05.2026 passed by learned Magistrate Section-30, Kabirwala was administrative/ executive in nature and, therefore, was not amenable to revisional jurisdiction. In such circumstances, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala, lacked jurisdiction to entertain the revision petition preferred by Allah Yar/respondent No.3 against the aforesaid order dated: 21.05.2026. The subsequent order dated 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala whereby the order of the learned Magistrate was interfered with and a District Standing Medical Board was constituted for re-examination of the injuries sustained by the injured, is consequently without lawful authority and jurisdiction and is, therefore, unsustainable in the eyes of law. Resultantly, the instant criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed and impugned order dated 15.06.2026 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kabirwala is hereby set aside. (Farooq Haider) Judge Approved for reporting. (Farooq Haider) Judge This order has been dictated, pronounced, prepared and signed on 02.11.2026. Javaid.S.
